extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, applicants, and agents (procedures for preliminary examination, pre-amendment communication, and collective examination)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules for conducting preliminary examination interviews, pre-amendment communications, and collective examination presentations between examiners and applicants/agents, including required records, timelines, participant eligibility, and post-interview processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral explanation of review results and grounds for rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Grounds for rejection based on the result of review shall be orally explained to the applicant during the interview; it is appropriate for the examiner to prepare the opinion on grounds for rejection in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is enough to state just the purpose of the grounds for rejection in the minutes to be used as references during or after interview. Examiner should bring a prepared opinion and explain deficiencies in the specification and other review results during the interview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner may suggest amendments but suggestions are non-binding
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is a proper way to resolve grounds for rejection, the examiner should actively suggest it during the interview, but the examiner shall not order or lead the applicant to follow the opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must explain that (1) the suggestion has no legal binding force, so final decision on amendment is the applicant's responsibility, and (2) the suggestion can be changed according to new prior art or evidence discovered after interview, or amendments after interview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation to secure proper scope of patent via amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner and the applicant shall make effort to consult possible amendment to resolve grounds for rejection discovered in the claimed invention and to secure proper scope of a patent based on advice on amendment and preliminary amendment proposed by each party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if examiner suggests amendment, applicant is free to decide final amendment. Both parties should attempt to agree on suggested amendments or language; if no agreement is reached, statement of amendment discussed can be omitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minutes/record of interview must be prepared and signed
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant and the examiner who participated in the interview shall prepare the minutes after finishing the interview and sign to prove checking the contents; copies can be distributed to the applicant upon request and minutes with sign shall be uploaded to Patent Net.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minutes must be computerized identically to the signed minutes and uploaded to examination history; the applicant's signed minutes should be added as an image to the report to indicate confirmation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of minutes / interview record
rubrics_metrics.description: In the minutes of interview, interview date, place, application number, title of invention, name of participant, examiner’s opinion on grounds for rejection, and suggestion of amendment discussed, etc. shall be stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For pre-amendment interview records, include result of pre-amendment review and discussed amendment. A summary of grounds for rejection may be sufficient if detailed opinion was explained orally during the interview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stating examiner's opinion on grounds for rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Opinion on grounds for rejection’ is about results of review of the claimed invention conducted by examiner considering requirements for patentability and deficiencies in the specification, and applicant’s response to it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner is recommended to prepare the opinion in advance and use it during the interview; the minutes may simply state the purpose of each ground so it can be used as a reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording applicant's argument in response to grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Argument of the applicant in response to the grounds for rejection stated by the examiner shall be described in the minutes/record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the guideline illustrate tabular or itemized description of article, claims affected, examiner position, and applicant response — include the applicant's reasoning and any factual/technical explanations given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stating suggested amendment and result of discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: If the suggestion of amendment proposed by the examiner to resolve grounds for rejection is discussed by the examiner and the applicant, the result of discussion shall be stated in the minutes of interview to make it a record of examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If agreement reached, state suggestion or actual language of amendment; recommended to state all contents discussed and agreed. If no agreement, statement of amendment discussed can be omitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finish of interview: criteria and allowed early termination
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner may finish the interview when the object is considered accomplished through explanations and when minutes are prepared. Examiner may finish by notifying the applicant in certain cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed early finish cases include: (i) interview goes beyond original purpose (main stream about patent system/process), (ii) applicant presents multiple preliminary amendment suggestions and asks examiner’s opinion on them, (iii) impossible to achieve agreement, (iv) interview time becomes unnecessarily long, (v) impossible to have effective interview. In such cases, it's sufficient to fill only matters discussed before finishing in the minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant's post-interview obligation: prepare written amendment/arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: An agent (if not, applicant) shall prepare written amendment to the specification or arguments after interview by reflecting applicant’s opinion on the amendment discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant wants to make amendment according to discussed amendment before start of substantive examination, submit written amendment (including written argument if necessary) within the prescribed period for submitting written amendment of preliminary examination (periods vary: e.g., 2 months from date to request preliminary examination; PPH/accelerated cases have different timelines). If difficulty arises, applicant may request extension by telephone. It is not permitted to present simplified arguments assuming the interview discussions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's post-interview duties: prepare interview report and upload minutes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Examiner shall prepare an interview report through the patent system after finishing the interview to add the minutes prepared during the interview to the examination history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The computerized contents must be identical to the minutes. The minutes with the applicant's signature should be made as an image and added to the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for starting substantive examination after interview
rubrics_metrics.description: The Examiner starts substantive examination based on contents (amendment discussed, etc.) stated in the minutes when the due date for start of substantive examination has arrived, but shall postpone until the period for submitting written amendment is expired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no written amendment is submitted within the period, the examiner commences substantive examination within prescribed intervals (e.g., within 2 months from date to request preliminary examination; accelerated cases differ). If written amendment filed before substantive examination, examiner can proceed within a month from receiving date. Examiner may make a different decision if new prior art or deficiencies are discovered after interview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and purpose of pre-amendment communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-amendment communication is a system to exchange opinions on draft amendment between applicants and examiners through an interview before submitting amendment in response to the outstanding rejection, to facilitate early allowance and more accurate examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process includes request, determination, carrying out interview (presentation/explanation), and submission of written amendment within the specified period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for pre-amendment communication (timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Among applications with grounds for rejection notified by an examiner, an application for which arguments including amendment or draft amendment are submitted before a month from the expiration date of the submission period for arguments may be eligible for pre-amendment communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request must be filed before one month from the expiration date of the period for submitting written amendment pursuant to the notice of grounds for rejection. Draft amendment should be submitted before or at the time of request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who can request and who may participate in pre-amendment communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants or agents are allowed to request pre-amendment communication. Participants may include the person in charge of the application (applicant representative, agent, subagent), and inventor if accompanied by an authorized respondent; agent must participate if the application is represented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications handled by an assistant examiner, the supervising examiner also should participate. Participants must be able to respond to office action responsibly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents allowable for pre-amendment interview
rubrics_metrics.description: All matters that help resolve grounds for rejection notified and secure proper scope of right based on draft amendment submitted by applicant can be discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may explain how amendment resolves grounds with technical explanations and may use samples or multimedia (photos/videos). Examiner may present preliminary opinion on whether draft resolves grounds and suggest amendments to resolve grounds or secure appropriate scope. Consultation should focus on resolving rejections and securing scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request procedure and scheduling for pre-amendment communication
rubrics_metrics.description: To file for pre-amendment communication, the applicant should use Patent-Ro form filling applicant name, application number, desired interview dates (three candidates), participants, contact number, and whether to submit draft amendment. Choose desired dates within 2–3 weeks from request, giving three candidate dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should accept or reject the request through Patent Net within 7 days from request date. If none of candidate dates work, examiner consults applicant by telephone to determine date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for examiner's determination to accept pre-amendment communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner should consider: (i) submission of draft amendment or arguments before/at time of request; (ii) request filed before one month from expiration of submission period; (iii) appropriate interview participants; (iv) presentation of three desired interview dates within 2–3 weeks; and (v) absence of inappropriate grounds (e.g., multiple pre-amendments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the request lacks one requirement but the deficiency can be resolved through discussion, examiner may accept ex officio without requiring form amendment or additional documents. If deficiency cannot be resolved, the request may be returned; applicant may refile after resolving deficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delay or cancellation rules for interview attendance
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant has an inevitable reason not to attend, examiner may allow one rescheduling among available dates within 15–21 days from request date after discussion; if examiner finds the reason inappropriate, the interview can be cancelled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only one opportunity to reschedule is normally provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner preparation for pre-amendment interview
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner should review whether grounds for rejection have been resolved or whether new grounds occur based on draft amendment, to an extent comparable to examination so examiner can explain clearly during the interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should participate with application documents, draft amendment, results of preview, written interview record and additional paper to write down matters consulted; recommended to prepare the result of pre-amendment review in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant presentation and use of materials in interview
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant should explain the draft amendment before or at the time of requesting review; applicant may use samples or multimedia (photo/video) to aid understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner can require interview materials in advance for examination. Applicant should mainly explain whether grounds for rejection are resolved and may provide technical explanations and prior art discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording and uploading of written interview record for pre-amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant and examiner should prepare written interview record after interview, sign to confirm, and upload the record with signatures to Patent-Net examination history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written interview record should include date, place, application number, title, participants, result of pre-amendment review, and discussed amendment. Examiner's written opinion may be prepared in advance but a summary in the record may suffice if detailed explanations were verbal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-pre-amendment applicant actions and submission deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Agent/applicant should prepare written amendment or argument reflecting consulted amendment after interview and submit it by the expiration date of the period for submitting written amendment; the applicant may freely amend regardless of the written interview record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not permitted to summarize written argument assuming what was discussed in the interview; amendments agreed during interview must be submitted by the normal deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's post-pre-amendment processing obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner should prepare an interview report via Patent Net to upload the written interview record and then conduct examination considering contents (consulted amendment, etc.) stated in the written interview record according to normal processes and periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computerized interview report must match the written interview record and include the applicant's signed image to indicate confirmation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collective examination purpose and overview
rubrics_metrics.description: Collective examination is a system to carry out examination collectively on a date an applicant desires for multiple applications (patent, utility model, trademark, design) relating to one product, enabling companies to obtain patents at a desired time for portfolio strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows establishing IP portfolio before product release; includes presentation for collective examination, formalities, and coordinated start/finish dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility criteria for collective examination (applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two or more applications of patent, utility model, trademark and design for which substantive examination has not started and which satisfy either (1) relate to one product and meet certain business/development criteria (practicing/preparing, export promotion, venture business/company selected under relevant acts, development of self-employed creative enterprises) or (2) related to development from identical national new technology development support project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent and utility model applications are limited to those for which a request for examination is made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may request collective examination and required representation
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for collective examination should be filed by the applicant; if more than two applicants exist, one must be selected as representative to file the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioner fills out the request form on Patent-Ro and attaches required certified documents; documents proving practicing or preparation may be shown to the examiner during presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheduling and content requirements for collective examination request
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioner should designate a presentation date (7–14 days after request), a desired start date (after 14 days from presentation date), and a finishing date within one year after three months from desired start date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If preliminary examination is wanted, it can be requested when filing for collective examination. After request, some applications may be withdrawn but not changed or added.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formality examination for collective examination requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Official in charge must confirm eligibility of applications and procedural requirements; if request does not satisfy requirements, petitioner must amend the request form within 6 days or the request may be denied or applications excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Official in charge selects presentation date in consultation with petitioner and examiner in charge and notifies petitioner of determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation content and decision for collective examination
rubrics_metrics.description: At presentation, petitioner explains how the applications relate to one product and provides technology/business information; official in charge and examiner in charge consult to determine which applications are eligible and agree on start/finish dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If preliminary examination was requested, the process for preliminary interview and after is the same as the procedures in Chapter 4 for preliminary examination.
